transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’ve been having trouble letting something go. For almost two years now, I’ve felt pretty certain that after a commission I did, some people in the ensemble started… undermining my work quietly. Like through schedule changes, where people were seated, small comments in rehearsal.  

They’ve shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it doesn’t really change what it feels like is happening.
Do you think these people are openly talking about undermining your work when you're not around?

Not openly, no. I don’t think they’d say it plainly like that. It’s more… the way things get arranged, certain seating choices, little comments in rehearsal. And then there are emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but I still can’t shake the feeling that it’s deliberate.
Do you think these beliefs about people undermining your work are something that you might be mistaken about, or do you feel absolutely certain that they are true?

I mean… I know it’s possible, technically, to be mistaken. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. It feels pretty certain that after that commission, a few of them started doing these small things—scheduling, seating, comments—to undercut me. The explanations they show me don’t really change that.
Do you have similar feelings of distrust or suspicion about people in other areas of your life, outside of this ensemble?

Not really in other areas. It’s mostly tied to the ensemble… after that commission. That’s where I keep seeing it — the schedule changes, seating decisions, small comments in rehearsal. I know people have shown me emails or notes to explain things, but it still feels intentional.
Have you ever felt this level of distrust or suspicion towards friends or family members outside of the ensemble?

No… not friends or family. I don’t really feel that with them. It’s been tied to the ensemble, after the commission—those schedule changes, seating decisions, little rehearsal comments. That’s where I can’t shake it.
Have you ever felt like people are out to harm or deceive you in general, outside of specific situations like the ensemble?

No… not in general. It’s really about the ensemble. Since that commission, I’ve just been sure a few of them are doing these little things—schedules, seating, comments—to undermine my work. Outside of that, I don’t really think people are out to get me.
Do you often find yourself wondering if someone is hiding something from you, even when there's no clear reason to think that?

Mostly just with them. I don’t walk around thinking everyone’s hiding things from me.

But with the ensemble… yes. Since that commission, I keep feeling like a few people are leaving things out or covering for each other—about schedules, seating, little comments in rehearsal. Even when they show me emails or notes, it still feels like there’s something underneath it.
Do you believe these people in the ensemble are specifically targeting you?

Yes… I think so. Not the whole ensemble, but a few people. Since the commission, it’s felt like they’ve been using schedule changes, seating choices, little rehearsal comments… just small things, but aimed at me, at my work. Even when they have explanations, it doesn’t really feel like the full truth.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your beliefs about the ensemble undermining your work might be incorrect, even if it feels certain to you?

I’ve… tried to consider that, yes. I know that’s probably why I’m here.

But honestly, for almost two years I haven’t been able to shake the feeling—really the certainty—that after the commission, a few of them started doing these things to undermine me. The schedule changes, seating choices, little comments in rehearsal… even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, it still doesn’t feel like the whole truth.
Do you generally assume that people have ulterior motives, even when you don't have any specific reason to think so?

Not generally, no. I don’t think that about everyone.

It’s more… with those few people in the ensemble. Since the commission, I can’t really shake the feeling that the schedule changes, seating decisions, little rehearsal comments—things like that—aren’t just random. Even when they show me emails or notes, it still feels like there’s something else behind it.
Have you ever had any moments where you doubted your beliefs about the ensemble undermining your work?

Sometimes, briefly. I can tell myself maybe it’s just normal ensemble politics or bad communication.

But it doesn’t last. I keep coming back to the same thing—that after the commission, certain schedule changes, seating choices, and comments in rehearsal were meant to undercut my work. Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, I still feel like there’s something else going on.
Do you think your belief about the ensemble undermining your work is based on facts or is it more of a gut feeling that you can't explain?

It’s… partly based on things that happened, I guess. The schedule changes, where people were seated, comments in rehearsals.

But the certainty of it—why I’m here—is that I can’t really let go of the feeling that those things were being used to undermine my work after the commission. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, it still doesn’t feel settled.
Have your beliefs about the ensemble undermining your work changed at all since they first started?

Not much, no.

It started after the commission, and… it’s stayed pretty much the same. I still keep seeing the schedule changes, the seating choices, the small rehearsal comments as connected. Like a few of them were using those things to undercut my work.

Even when they’ve shown me emails or notes explaining it, I haven’t really been able to shake it.
Do you think there's any possibility that your interpretation of these events is not accurate?

I guess there’s a possibility, yes. I can say that.

But… I’m here because I haven’t really been able to believe that’s the case. For almost two years I keep coming back to the same certainty—that after the commission, a few people were using the schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to quietly undermine my work.

Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, it still doesn’t really feel like the whole story.
Are these thoughts about the ensemble undermining your work affecting your ability to function in your daily life?

A little, yes.

Mostly it makes rehearsals and emails harder than they probably should be. I reread things, decisions people make, and sometimes I ask for more clarification than I used to.

But I haven’t lost work over it or stopped taking care of myself. It’s more… it takes up energy.
Have these thoughts about the ensemble undermining your work affected your relationships with friends or family?

Not really, no.

I mean… outside of the ensemble issue, things are mostly normal. I still meet deadlines, keep composing, run most mornings. And at home, with my wife, things are basically steady. So… I wouldn’t say it’s really damaged those relationships.
Have these thoughts about the ensemble undermining your work caused you to avoid any activities or situations?

Not really avoid, no.

I mean… I still go to rehearsals, still answer the emails, still do the work. It just takes more out of me than it used to. I reread decisions and sometimes ask people to clarify things, but I haven’t stopped doing anything important.
Have these thoughts about the ensemble undermining your work caused you significant distress?

I mean… some, I guess. I wouldn’t call it overwhelming.

It bothers me, and I think about it more than I’d like. But I’m still managing.
Do you think your beliefs about the ensemble undermining your work would change if everyone involved told you directly that they are not trying to undermine you?

Honestly… probably not completely.

I mean, they have shown me emails and notes before, explaining schedule changes or seating decisions, and I can understand what they’re saying on the surface. But it still feels like there’s something underneath it. Like after that commission, a few people started doing these small things that add up.

So if everyone said it directly… I’d listen, but I don’t know that it would make the feeling go away.
Do you think your beliefs about the ensemble undermining your work are based on reality?

Yes. I mean… I know how it sounds, but yes, I think it’s based on what’s actually been happening.

After that commission, certain things changed — schedule shifts, seating choices, small comments in rehearsal. They can show me emails or explanations, and I get that there’s an official reason. I just don’t think that’s the whole reality of it.
